section: what a long-context benchmark has to separate
text: Whether the model uses what it accepted is a separate question, and long-context benchmarks ask it at three levels of difficulty: Find: retrieve one stated fact (needle in a haystack, single-needle RULER tasks).
label: core

text: Needle in a haystack: the test that was solved by its own design Greg Kamradt's open-source test ( LLMTest_NeedleInAHaystack , November 2023) plants one sentence in a long run of essays and asks for it back, sweeping context length on one axis and needle depth on the other; the result is the familiar green-and-red heatmap.

section: ruler: from one needle to thirteen tasks, and "effective length"
text: RULER: from one needle to thirteen tasks, and "effective length" NVIDIA's RULER ( Hsieh et al., v3 , April 2024) kept the needle's convenience (synthetic, any length, exact grading) and widened the tasks to 13 in four categories: Retrieval: eight needle variants: one or several keys, several values for one key, several queries, distractor needles, keys that are words, numbers or UUIDs.
label: core

text: Click a block to see it. worked examples (first user turn) user request model reply (written by GPT-4o) the repeated request its replies (the needles) final question The final turn Both needles repeat the request word for word ("write a short scene in a play about blueberries"), so finding them is easy; the task is telling the 1st from the 2nd and copying the right one exactly, with the random string in front.

section: grade a real mrcr item
text: The grader score = 0 if the reply does not start with the prefix, else 2M ⁄ (|reply| + |target|) M characters in the matching blocks SequenceMatcher finds between the reply and the target, both with the prefix removed: it takes the longest common substring, then recurses on the pieces to its left and right autojunk when the target has 200 or more characters, any character occurring more than 1% of its length (plus one) cannot start a match; spaces and common letters are "popular" here, which is why near-copies still score close to 1 and unrelated texts close to 0 Try: the presets, then edit the reply: delete a line, change a name, drop the prefix's last character.

key: plus one) from starting a match
